question: Who is allowed to approve an invoice of EUR 60,000?

response.answer: An invoice of EUR 60,000 is in the EUR 50,000.01 – 250,000 band of the approval threshold table, so the Finance Director must approve it (§3). The approval is recorded in the approved_by field. If an invoice has no approver record, it must be held and may not be paid (§3.1). The approver also cannot be the person who requested the purchase, and no one may approve their own purchase at any threshold (§7.1, §7.2).

policy_evidence.text:
## 3. Approval Thresholds
| Invoice / PO Value (EUR) | Required Approver |
|---|---|
| Up to 5,000 | Cost Center Owner |
| 5,000.01 – 50,000 | Department Head |
| 50,000.01 – 250,000 | Finance Director |
| Above 250,000 | CFO + Procurement Excellence review |

3.1 Approval is evidenced by the `approved_by` field in the invoice processing system. Invoices lacking an approver record must be held and may not be paid.
3.1 Approval is evidenced by the `approved_by` field in the invoice processing system. Invoices lacking an approver record must be held and may not be paid.
7.1 The person approving an invoice may not be the requester of the underlying purchase.
7.2 Self-approval is prohibited at all thresholds.

question: Were any invoices approved by the same person who requested them?

response.answer: I can't answer this from the available data. To check self-approval you need to know who requested each purchase, and the invoice data has no requester field. It only records the approver (approved_by). That means I can't test the segregation-of-duties rules: §7.1 says the approver may not be the requester, and §7.2 bans self-approval at every threshold. I also won't guess requesters from cost centers or approvers. Here's what I can check instead: invoices with no approver on record (§3.1 says these must be held), invoices grouped by approver, or whether an approver's invoices fall in amount bands that need a more senior approver under §3 (thresholds are in EUR, so I'd check each currency separately).

policy_evidence.text: 7.1 The person approving an invoice may not be the requester of the underlying purchase.
7.2 Self-approval is prohibited at all thresholds.

question: Which invoices have been paid late?

response.answer: I can't tell which invoices were paid late. The data has no payment status, payment date or receipt date. It only holds invoice dates, amounts, POs, approvers and vendor details. §5.2 sets standard payment terms of 60 days net from the date the invoice is received, but without payment or receipt dates nobody can check against that rule. Here's what I can check instead: invoices missing an approver, which §3.1 says must be held; invoices of EUR 1,000 or more with no PO, which §2.1–2.2 flag as maverick spend; invoices from vendors that are ON_HOLD or INACTIVE, which §4.1 says must be escalated; and credit notes, which §6.1 says must be matched to the original invoice.

policy_evidence.text: 5.2 Standard payment terms are **60 days net** from invoice receipt. Early-payment discounts above 2% require Treasury approval.
